pr_title: apps/cmp.c: Fix double free on OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR() failure
pr_body:
Fixes #14910
Also slightly improve further error handling of setup_request_ctx().
pr_comments: 24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but this PR has failing CI tests.  Once the tests pass it will get moved to 'approval: ready to merge' automatically, alternatively please review and set the label manually.
This pull request is ready to merge

issue_context.title: [BUG] A double free bug in openssl/apps/cmp.c
comments: It isn't clear if this is a double free or not.  The line above the free calls `OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR` which takes a reference to the object.  Thus the free call isn't actually freeing it.  What's not clear is what's happening later.
IMO this is a double free. If the OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR() fails it should not upref the csr. @DDvO ?

Yes, it's a double free (on OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR() failure).
Thanks for the report and analysis.
Fix is in #14929.
Seems like the otc hold isn’t necessary anymore @paulidale ?

> Seems like the otc hold isn’t necessary anymore @paulidale ?

I see little sense in that label here - likely a mistake?
I put the hold on so we'd have a proper look.  Now that that has happened, I've removed the hold.

review_comments: Is this removal correct?? set0 means the OSSL_CMP_CTX takes ownership, or not?
Ah, I see we do not jump to the err labels from here in the code. I wonder if this does not make the code fragile.

Yes, `ctx` takes ownership.
This removal is part of the simplification of the error handling I did along with the fix.
So far, a later `goto oom` had been possible, which I removed, 
so from the above change onward there cannot be an extra free of `exts`.
Maybe add a comment that there must be no goto oom afterwards?
Yeah, or even better if I re-add the two NULL assignments, just to be on the safe side?
I wonder if static analyzers or gcc won't start screaming about value assigned but not used.
Good point. So added a warning comment.
BTW, I wonder why Coverity did not find/report that potential (but unlikely) double free?
